efile.text: Employers are required to electronically file and pay Ohio employer and school district withholding taxes either through OH|TAX eServices or through the Ohio Treasurer of State or by any other electronic means prescribed by the tax commissioner. See Ohio Adm. Code 5703-7-19.

returns.name: Ohio IT 501, Return for Income Tax Withheld
contents: Reports and pays the Ohio income tax withheld for the period; not required if there is no Ohio liability for the period. Quarterly and monthly filers file it with their payment on the printed due dates; partial-weekly filers pay by EFT.
Filing all IT 501s does not complete the requirement: the annual reconciliation is also required.

returns.name: Ohio IT 941, Annual Reconciliation of Income Tax Withheld
contents: Due January 31 of the following year, or within 15 days after the business is discontinued; total tax withheld must equal the W-2s and 1099s submitted.
All employers upload W-2/1099 information electronically through OH|TAX eServices; school district withholding is reconciled on SD 141.

deposits.interpretation: Ohio sets the filing frequency each calendar year from the COMBINED state and school district tax withheld in the 12 months ended June 30 of the preceding year (estimated at registration): $2,000 or less QUARTERLY; more than $2,000 but less than $84,000 MONTHLY; $84,000 or more PARTIAL-WEEKLY (state tax only; payments by EFT through the Ohio Treasurer of State within three banking days of the end of each partial-weekly period; the two periods each week are Saturday-Tuesday and Wednesday-Friday, chosen by the payroll day, and a period never runs from one year into the next). The look-back amount supplied must be the COMBINED state and school district figure. Ohio prints its 2026 due dates, so the profile holds them as the agency's calendar: every monthly period (December 2025 wages January 15, 2026 through December 2026 wages January 15, 2027), every quarter (Q4 2025 February 2, 2026 through Q4 2026 February 1, 2027), and all 105 partial-weekly periods of 2026 with their due dates (a period ending on a holiday week moves, e.g. Monday January 19 is skipped). Pay dates in any other year draw state_calendar_not_published. THE $100,000 RULE IS NOT MODELLED: Ohio applies it to the combined state and school district withholding for a payroll and requires the Ohio portion the first banking day after, but this layer sees only the state tax, so it cannot test the combined amount; a payroll that reaches $100,000 combined needs the next-banking-day payment by hand. School district withholding (return SD 101) is a separate tax and is not deposited here.

enrollment: Register online through OH|TAX eServices within 15 days of when withholding liability begins; the FEIN, legal name and e-mail address are needed; the account number is used for both employer and school district withholding.
Partial-weekly EFT payments go through the Ohio Treasurer of State.

returns.name: Quarterly contribution and wage report (or payroll and wage report for reimbursing employers)
contents: Filed not later than the last day of the first month following the close of the calendar quarter (April 30, July 31, October 31, January 31) (ORC 4141.20(B), (C)).
The forfeiture for failing to file a complete report when due is 0.25 percent of total remuneration reported (ORC 4141.20).
